title: Agent State & Execution Models
description: Study explicit state machines, durable state and replay, context versus long-term memory, and termination and progress invariants. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Explicit state machines
lessons.description: Draw the states and guards for a booking workflow with cancellation.
lessons.conceptOverview: A state machine names allowed states and transitions so orchestration can be validated without interpreting free-form text. Store task inputs, current step and outcomes separately, and reject transitions that violate invariants.
lessons.whyItMatters: Guarded transitions make workflow authority explicit.

lessons.title: Durable state and replay
lessons.description: Describe the operation identifier and reconciliation step needed on restart.
lessons.conceptOverview: Durable execution records enough state to resume after failure. Replay must distinguish already-completed side effects from pending work; rerunning code is not equivalent to safely repeating external operations.
lessons.whyItMatters: Recovery must reconcile external effects before retrying.

lessons.title: Context versus long-term memory
lessons.description: Design memory records with source, confidence and expiry fields.
lessons.conceptOverview: Context is the information supplied to the current decision; durable memory is stored information retrieved across decisions. Track provenance and expiry, and keep user facts separate from unverified model notes.
lessons.whyItMatters: Unverified observations must not become confirmed user facts.

lessons.title: Termination and progress invariants
lessons.description: Define a repetition detector and an escalation condition.
lessons.conceptOverview: Bounded agents require step limits, time budgets and explicit completion criteria. Detect repeated states or tool outcomes so apparent activity cannot consume resources indefinitely without progress.
lessons.whyItMatters: Termination needs measurable progress and resource bounds.
